evaluation: Balanced Plain English Benchmark v2 — A/B quality evaluation
per_run_scores_note: Per-run rubric scores were not written to disk. Only the aggregate figures below were reported by the evaluation. They cannot be independently recomputed from the preserved artifacts, unlike the token figures.

blinding.detail: Each benchmark run was told its own condition and echoed it into its response header, e.g. 'Condition: OFF (Balanced Plain English disabled)'. The A/B labels were anonymised and the A/B ordering was randomised, but the condition remained recoverable from the response body in every pair.

reconciliation_note: No preserved artifact — including the original benchmark brief (BPE_Token_Efficiency_Evidence_v2.md) — records a head-to-head win count in either direction. A prior version of this file published an arithmetic-derived split (OFF 10 / ON 6), reasoning that the averages and medians 'require' that split if every non-tied pair differed by exactly one rubric point. That single-point-gap assumption (previously recorded here as max_observed_gap_points: 1) is itself not a preserved fact: 'material_quality_differences: 0' only shows every pair's gap stayed under the evaluator's materiality threshold, not that every non-tied gap was exactly 1 point. Because the derivation depends on an unverified assumption, off_wins/on_wins have been withdrawn rather than republished under either labeling. The verified quality figures are the averages, medians, ties, material-difference count, and task completion above.
supported_claim: The A/B quality evaluation detected no material quality difference across the 20 paired tests, and all 40 responses completed the task.
unsupported_claims: head-to-head win counts in either direction
every non-tied difference was a single rubric point
